comps.label: C1
comps.reason: Plasma-derived immune globulin with owned plasma collection centers; a different product and manufacturing model from Akebia's kidney-anemia drugs.

comps.label: C2
comps.reason: Generic injectables, inhalers and OTC products; generic and consumer lines differ from Akebia's branded prescription drugs for dialysis patients.

comps.label: C3
comps.reason: Specialty chemical ingredients sold to formulators and manufacturers; not a prescription drug business.

comps.label: C4
comps.reason: Consumer protein shakes and sports nutrition sold through retailers; no prescription drugs or clinical customers.

comps.label: C5
comps.reason: Branded prescription drugs for rare diseases, sold through specialty pharmacies and distributors, with partner sales abroad, as Akebia does.

comps.label: C6
comps.reason: Orthopedic devices and biologics sold to surgeons and clinics; medical devices rather than prescription drugs.

comps.label: C7
comps.reason: Wearable glucose monitoring devices sold to patients and pharmacies; devices, not prescription drugs.

comps.label: C8
comps.reason: Free physician networking platform monetized by pharma marketing and trial services; not a drug seller.

comps.label: C9
comps.reason: Implantable heart valves and hemodynamic monitors sold to hospitals; devices for cardiac surgery.

comps.label: C10
comps.reason: Orthopedic implants, bracing and rehabilitation devices sold to surgeons; device business.

comps.label: C11
comps.reason: Branded prescription medicine for rare neurological disorders, sold via specialty pharmacies and distributors, with licensing royalties abroad.

comps.label: C12
comps.reason: Surgical devices, implants and instruments sold to hospitals and surgeons; device business.

comps.label: C13
comps.reason: Gastrointestinal prescription drugs earning royalties from partners and sold through pharmacies, closely matching Akebia's licensing model.

comps.label: C14
comps.reason: Branded specialty pain drugs sold to specialist and surgical customers under FDA approval; drug franchise, though hospital-focused and with a device line.

comps.label: C15
comps.reason: Single branded oral drug for a specialist-treated disease, sold to specialty distributors with licensed partners selling abroad.

comps.label: C16
comps.reason: Oral prescription medicines for specialist-treated blood disorders, sold to specialty pharmacies and distributors, with ex-US partner royalties.

comps.label: C17
comps.reason: Branded prescription CNS drugs sold to wholesalers and pharmacies under FDA approval, a US specialty pharma model like Akebia's.

comps.label: C18
comps.reason: Broad hospital medical devices including catheters and surgical instruments; devices rather than prescription drugs.

comps.label: C19
comps.reason: Branded snacks and shakes sold through grocery and mass retail; consumer food, not prescription drugs.
